arguments.content:
---
name: slack-api
description: Interact with the Slack API — send and update messages, reply in threads, list channels, read channel history, upload files, search messages, and call any Slack Web API method (chat.postMessage, conversations.list, conversations.history, files.uploadV2, search.messages, users.info, reactions.add, etc.) via dependency-free Node.js scripts. Use when the user wants to post to Slack, retrieve Slack messages or channel data, or automate Slack workflows from the command line. Requires a Slack bot or user token.
---

# Slack API

## Overview

Dependency-free Node.js scripts (native `fetch`, Node 18+) for the Slack Web API, plus reference docs for endpoints and message formatting. All scripts read the token from the `SLACK_TOKEN` env var, print clean `Success:`/`Failure:` lines, and exit non-zero on error so an agent can act on the result.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 18+.
- A Slack token with the required scopes, exported as an environment variable — never pass it as a command-line argument:
  `export SLACK_TOKEN=xoxb-...` (bot token) or `xoxp-...` (user token).
- The bot/user must be a member of the target channel (or join it first with `conversations.join`, which needs the `channels:join` scope).
- Required scopes per method: [references/api.md](references/api.md).

## Quick Start

Call any Web API method with the generic script:

```bash
SLACK_TOKEN=xoxb-... node scripts/slack_api.cjs chat.postMessage '{"channel":"C1234567890","text":"Hello from Gemini CLI!"}'
```

Responses print as truncated JSON (~4000 chars max) to avoid overflowing the context window.

## Common Tasks

### Send a message

```bash
node scripts/post_message.cjs <channel> "<message text>"
```

- Channel: ID (`C123...`) or name (`#general`).
- Reply in a thread: add `--thread_ts <parent-ts>`.
- Rich message: `--blocks '<json>'` (see [references/messages.md](references/messages.md)).
- Override sender (bot tokens): `--username <name> --icon_emoji <emoji>`.

### List channels

```bash
node scripts/list_channels.cjs [--limit 100] [--include-archived]
```

Prints `id`, `#name`, member count, and topic. If more results exist, prints the `--cursor` to fetch the next page.

### Read channel history

```bash
node scripts/fetch_history.cjs <channel> [--limit 50] [--oldest <ts>] [--latest <ts>] [--inclusive] [--cursor <cursor>]
```

Prints newest-first messages with `ts`, sender, and truncated text. Use `--oldest`/`--latest` (float epoch seconds, e.g. `1710000000.123456`) for time windows.

### Reply in a thread

Find the parent message `ts` via `fetch_history.cjs`, then post with `--thread_ts`. To read replies:

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.cjs conversations.replies '{"channel":"C123","ts":"1710000000.123456"}'
```

### Upload a file

```bash
node scripts/upload_file.cjs <channel> <path/to/file> [--comment "text"] [--title "Title"] [--filename name]
```

Implements the current two-step `files.uploadV2` flow (`files.getUploadURLExternal` → CDN upload → `files.completeUploadExternal`), then reports the permalink.

### Any other method (search, users, reactions, update, delete, ephemeral, ...)

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.cjs <method> '<json-args>'
```

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.cjs search.messages '{"query":"deploy failed","count":10}'
node scripts/slack_api.cjs users.info '{"user":"U1234567890"}'
node scripts/slack_api.cjs reactions.add '{"channel":"C123","name":"+1","timestamp":"1710000000.123456"}'
```

Full endpoint catalog, scopes, pagination, rate limits, and error codes: [references/api.md](references/api.md).

## References (read only when needed)

- [references/api.md](references/api.md) — endpoint catalog with required scopes, response envelope, cursor pagination, rate limits, common error codes, and examples.
- [references/messages.md](references/messages.md) — text formatting (mrkdwn), Block Kit JSON, threads, and message limits.

## Error Handling

- Scripts exit non-zero and print `Failure: <reason>`; read that before retrying.
- Common Slack errors: `invalid_auth` (bad token), `missing_scope` (token lacks a scope — the error lists `needed`/`provided`), `channel_not_found`, `not_in_channel` (join first: `node scripts/slack_api.cjs conversations.join '{"channel":"C123"}'`), `rate_limited` (honor the `Retry-After` header), `invalid_blocks` (malformed Block Kit).
- Do not retry on `invalid_auth`, `missing_scope`, `channel_not_found`, or `invalid_blocks` — fix the input first. Retry with backoff on `rate_limited` or network errors.

# Slack Web API Reference

## Table of Contents

- [Authentication & tokens](#authentication--tokens)
- [Response envelope](#response-envelope)
- [Pagination](#pagination)
- [Rate limits](#rate-limits)
- [Common error codes](#common-error-codes)
- [Endpoints](#endpoints)
- [Examples](#examples)

## Authentication & tokens

- Bot token `xoxb-...` (recommended for automation) or user token `xoxp-...`. All scripts read it from the `SLACK_TOKEN` env var and send `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- The token must have the scope required by the method (listed per endpoint below). On `missing_scope`, the error response includes `needed` and `provided` scopes.
- Chat methods require the bot to be a member of the target channel unless the workspace allows public-channel posting.

## Response envelope

Every method returns JSON with a top-level `ok` flag:

```json
{ "ok": true, "channel": "C123", "ts": "1710000000.123456" }
```

On failure:

```json
{ "ok": false, "error": "not_in_channel", "response_metadata": { "messages": ["..."] } }
```

Never rely on HTTP status alone — always check `ok`.

## Pagination

- List-style endpoints (`conversations.list`, `conversations.history`, `conversations.replies`, `search.messages`, `users.list`) paginate with `cursor` + `limit`.
- The response contains `response_metadata.next_cursor`. Pass it as `cursor` in the next call; an empty string means there are no more pages.
- Max `limit`: 200 for `conversations.list`/`conversations.history`/`conversations.replies`, 100 for `users.list`, 1000 for `search.messages` (`count`).

## Rate limits

- Slack applies per-method tiers (approximate): Tier 1 ~1+ req/sec (`chat.postMessage`, `chat.update`, `reactions.add`), Tier 2 ~20+/min (`conversations.history`, `conversations.replies`, `users.info`, `files.info`), Tier 3 ~50+/min (`conversations.list`, `users.list`, `conversations.info`), Tier 4 ~100+/min (`search.messages`).
- On `rate_limited` the HTTP response includes a `Retry-After` header (seconds). Wait and retry, max 3 attempts with backoff.
- Batch reads (larger `limit`, cursors) to minimize the number of calls.

## Common error codes

| error | meaning | action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `invalid_auth` | bad or expired token | fix the token |
| `missing_scope` | token lacks the required scope | add the scope from the table below |
| `not_authed` / `account_inactive` | auth problem | check the token |
| `channel_not_found` | bad channel id/name | verify the channel exists; prefer the channel ID |
| `not_in_channel` | bot is not in the channel | `conversations.join` (needs `channels:join`) or invite the bot |
| `is_archived` | channel is archived | unarchive or use another channel |
| `invalid_blocks` / `invalid_arguments` | malformed payload | fix the JSON |
| `rate_limited` | too many requests | honor `Retry-After` |
| `too_many_attachments` | message payload too large | trim blocks/attachments |

## Endpoints

### chat.postMessage

Send a message. Scope: `chat:write`.
Params: `channel` (required), `text` (required unless `blocks`), `blocks`, `thread_ts`, `reply_broadcast`, `username`, `icon_emoji`, `icon_url`, `mrkdwn`, `link_names`, `unfurl_links`, `unfurl_media`.
Returns: `{ ok, channel, ts, message }`.

- If both `text` and `blocks` are sent, `text` is the fallback shown in notifications and accessibility tools.
- Reply in a thread by passing the parent ts as `thread_ts`; `reply_broadcast: true` also posts a copy to the channel.

### chat.update

Edit a message. Scope: `chat:write`. Params: `channel`, `ts` (required), `text`/`blocks`, `link_names`, `parse`.
Returns: `{ ok, channel, ts, message }`.

### chat.delete

Delete a message. Scope: `chat:write`. Params: `channel`, `ts`.
Returns: `{ ok, channel, ts }`.

### chat.postEphemeral

Post a message visible only to one user. Scope: `chat:write`. Params: `channel`, `user`, `text`/`blocks`, `thread_ts`.
Returns: `{ ok, message_ts }`.

### conversations.list

List channels. Scopes: `channels:read`, plus `groups:read`, `im:read`, `mpim:read` depending on `types`.
Params: `types` (comma-separated: `public_channel`, `private_channel`, `mpim`, `im`; default `public_channel`), `limit` (max 200), `cursor`, `exclude_archived`, `team_id`.
Returns: `channels[]` — each with `id`, `name`, `is_channel`, `is_private`, `is_archived`, `is_member`, `num_members`, `topic.value`, `purpose.value`.

### conversations.history

Fetch channel history (public, private, or DM). Scopes: `channels:history`, `groups:history`, `im:history`, `mpim:history`.
Params: `channel`, `limit` (max 200), `cursor`, `oldest`, `latest` (float epoch seconds), `inclusive` (default false).
Returns: `messages[]` newest-first, `has_more`, `response_metadata.next_cursor`.

Message fields: `ts`, `user`, `bot_id`, `text`, `subtype`, `thread_ts`, `reply_count`, `reply_users_count`, `reactions[]` (`name`, `count`, `users`), `files[]`, `attachments[]`, `blocks[]`.

### conversations.replies

Fetch thread replies. Scopes: same as history. Params: `channel`, `ts` (parent message ts), `limit`, `cursor`, `oldest`, `latest`, `inclusive`.
Returns: `messages[]` — the first item is the parent message (with `reply_count`), followed by replies newest-first.

### conversations.info

Channel metadata. Scopes: `channels:read` (or `groups:read`/`im:read`/`mpim:read`). Params: `channel`, `include_num_members`.
Returns: `channel{...}`.

### conversations.open

Open a DM (or resume an existing one). Scopes: `im:write` (or `mpim:write` for group DMs). Params: `users` (comma-separated) or `channel` (existing DM id), `return_im`.
Returns: `channel{ id, ... }` — use the returned channel id with `chat.postMessage`.

### conversations.join / leave / archive / unarchive / rename

Membership and admin operations. `conversations.join`: scope `channels:join`, params `channel`. Archive/rename: scope `channels:manage`.

### files.uploadV2 (two-step upload)

Upload files. Scope: `files:write`. Use `scripts/upload_file.cjs`, which implements this flow:

1. `files.getUploadURLExternal` — params: `filename`, `length` (bytes), `alt_txt`. Returns: `upload_url`, `file_id`.
2. POST the file bytes to `upload_url` with `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`.
3. `files.completeUploadExternal` — params: `files: [{ id: file_id, title }]`, `channel_id`, `initial_comment`. Returns: `files[]` with `id`, `title`.
4. Optional: `files.info` (scope `files:read`) for `permalink`, `url_private`.

### search.messages

Search messages. Scope: `search:read`. Params: `query`, `count` (max 1000), `page`, `sort` (`score` or `timestamp`), `sort_dir`.
Returns: `messages.matches[]` with `channel{id,name}`, `ts`, `user`, `text`, `permalink`, `blocks`.
Query syntax: `from:@user`, `in:#channel`, `after:YYYY-MM-DD`, `before:YYYY-MM-DD`, `has::emoji:`, quoted phrases for exact matches.

### users.info / users.list

User lookup. Scope: `users:read`. `users.info` params: `user`, `include_locale`. Returns: `user{ id, name, real_name, is_bot, deleted, profile{ display_name, email, image_* } }`. `users.list` params: `limit` (max 100), `cursor`, `include_locale`.

### reactions.add / reactions.remove / reactions.get

Emoji reactions. Scopes: `reactions:write` (add/remove), `reactions:read` (get). `reactions.add` params: `channel`, `name` (no colons), `timestamp` (message ts).

### chat.getPermalink

Get a message permalink. Scope: none required beyond auth. Params: `channel`, `message_ts`. Returns: `permalink`.

## Examples

Generic script:

```bash
SLACK_TOKEN=xoxb-... node scripts/slack_api.cjs chat.postMessage \
  '{"channel":"C123","text":"hi","thread_ts":"1710000000.123456"}'
```

curl equivalent:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"channel":"C123","text":"hi"}'
```

# Message Formatting in Slack

## Table of Contents

- [Plain text & mrkdwn](#plain-text--mrkdwn)
- [Escaping](#escaping)
- [Block Kit](#block-kit)
- [Legacy attachments](#legacy-attachments)
- [Threads](#threads)
- [Limits](#limits)

## Plain text & mrkdwn

When sending with `text` only (no `blocks`), Slack renders lightweight markdown:

- `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `~strike~`, `` `code` ``, ``` ``preformatted`` ``` (triple backticks)
- `> blockquote` at the start of a line
- Links: `<https://example.com>` or `<https://example.com|Click here>`
- Emoji: `:tada:`, `:white_check_mark:`
- Mentions: `<@U12345>` (user), `<#C12345|general>` (channel), `<!channel>`, `<!here>`, `<!everyone>`, `<!subteam^S123|@team>`
- Newlines: `\n` in the JSON string

## Escaping

Slack does not auto-escape `text` in `chat.postMessage`. Escape user-supplied content so it cannot inject markup: `&` → `&`, `<` → `<`, `>` → `>`. This matters for mrkdwn text objects too. `plain_text` objects display as-is (no markup parsing), but still escape when the content is user input.

## Block Kit

`blocks` is a JSON array that builds rich messages. Max 50 blocks per message. Always include `text` as a plain fallback alongside blocks.

### Common blocks

Section with optional accessory:

```json
{
  "type": "section",
  "text": { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Title*\nBody text" },
  "accessory": {
    "type": "button",
    "text": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Click", "emoji": true },
    "action_id": "btn_1",
    "url": "https://example.com"
  }
}
```

Divider:

```json
{ "type": "divider" }
```

Header (text max 150 chars):

```json
{ "type": "header", "text": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Title", "emoji": true } }
```

Context (max 10 elements):

```json
{ "type": "context", "elements": [ { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "_Posted by the deploy bot_" } ] }
```

Image:

```json
{ "type": "image", "image_url": "https://example.com/logo.png", "alt_text": "logo" }
```

Input (modals only):

```json
{
  "type": "input",
  "label": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Label" },
  "element": { "type": "plain_text_input", "action_id": "inp_1" }
}
```

### Text objects

- `mrkdwn`: `{ "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "..." }` — parses formatting; escape `&`, `<`, `>` in user content.
- `plain_text`: `{ "type": "plain_text", "text": "...", "emoji": true }` — no formatting.

### Interactive elements

`button`, `datepicker`, `static_select`, `multi_static_select`, `plain_text_input`, `overflow`, `radio_buttons`, `checkboxes`, `timepicker`. Buttons/selects require `action_id`; buttons with `url` open links, otherwise they trigger interactive workflows.

## Legacy attachments

`attachments` predate blocks but are still supported:

```json
{
  "attachments": [
    {
      "color": "#36a64f",
      "title": "Deploy complete",
      "text": "v2.4.1 shipped to production",
      "fields": [ { "title": "Env", "value": "prod", "short": true } ],
      "footer": "CI",
      "mrkdwn_in": ["text", "fields"]
    }
  ]
}
```

Prefer blocks for new messages; use attachments only for color/field layouts that blocks do not cover.

## Threads

- Reply to a thread by passing `thread_ts` (the parent message ts) to `chat.postMessage`; the response `ts` is the reply's own ts.
- `reply_broadcast: true` also posts a copy to the channel.
- Read replies with `conversations.replies` (`channel` + parent `ts`).
- In history, a message with `thread_ts` equal to its own `ts` is a parent; others are replies. `reply_count` shows how many replies exist.

## Limits

- Blocks per message: max 50.
- Block text object: max 3,000 characters.
- Header text: max 150 characters.
- Context elements: max 10.
- Input label: max 2,000 characters.
- Button label: max 75 characters.
- `text` (non-block message): up to 40,000 characters.
